title: Cryptography Fundamentals: Symmetric, Public-Key, Key Exchange and MACs
oneLiner: What encryption, MACs, signatures and key exchange each guarantee, AES-GCM, RSA and Diffie-Hellman by hand, forward secrecy, and post-quantum crypto.
keyTakeaway: Encryption gives confidentiality, a MAC gives integrity with a shared key, and a signature gives integrity anyone can check plus non-repudiation. Real systems are hybrid: a key exchange or public-key step sets up a symmetric key, and authenticated encryption such as AES-GCM carries the data. Use library APIs, secure random numbers and unique nonces; never build your own.
explanation:
HTTPS, SSH, JWTs, code signing and disk encryption are all built from a handful of cryptographic tools. This lesson explains what each one guarantees and what it doesn't, so you can pick the right library call and spot a design that is missing a piece.

You can try a small Diffie-Hellman exchange and a toy RSA key pair in the page, then see how TLS combines them. The code samples were run to get the output shown.
